title: Business registration with the Business Registration Service
why: A registered business can open a business bank account and sign contracts in its own name, and many funders ask for it.
when_to_get_help: If you are choosing between a business name and a limited company, an accountant or lawyer can explain the difference.

title: KRA PIN for the business
why: The business needs its own PIN to pay tax, and funders and banks often ask for it.

title: Tax compliance certificate
why: Some funders and tenders ask for proof that the business is up to date with its taxes.

title: County business permit
why: Counties require a permit to trade from a premises, and it is renewed regularly.

title: Employer registrations (NSSF, SHIF, Housing Levy)
why: A business with employees has to register as an employer and make deductions for them.
when_to_get_help: An accountant can set up payroll deductions correctly.

title: Data protection registration with the ODPC
why: A business that collects or stores personal data may need to register as a data controller or processor.
institution: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner

title: Bank account in the business name
why: Keeps business money separate from personal money, and lenders ask for it.

title: Founders' or shareholders' agreement
why: Sets out who owns what and what happens if someone leaves.
when_to_get_help: A lawyer should draft or review this before anyone signs.

title: Company registered with BRS, if not yet a company
Directors and shareholders updated with BRS
Term sheet
why: Records the main terms both sides have agreed before the full agreement is drafted.
when_to_get_help: A lawyer should draft or review this before anyone signs.

title: Investment agreement or shareholders' agreement
when_to_get_help: A lawyer should draft or review this before anyone signs.

title: Share allotment and register updates with BRS
Tax and stamp duty questions referred to an accountant
when_to_get_help: An accountant should advise on tax and stamp duty for this deal.

title: Engagement letter with scope and fees
Group registered, for example as a self-help group
why: Some funds lend only to registered groups, and a registered group can open an account in its own name.
